moments.text: Ravi Menon, Operations Manager at a 40-truck logistics firm in Pune, picks up on the second ring. "Yeah? Two minutes. What is this about?"

options.text: I'll keep it short — we help logistics teams cut delivery delays. Worth ten minutes?
options.feedback: You pitched before you knew anything about his operation. He has no reason to care yet.

options.text: Fair. One question — what's costing you more right now, late deliveries or fuel?
options.feedback: Strong. You earned the next thirty seconds by making it about him instead of your product.

options.text: Are you the person who decides on operations software?
options.feedback: Too early. You asked for authority before you had given him any reason to talk.

moments.text: He exhales. "Both, honestly. Trucks are running late and diesel is eating us alive."

options.text: That's exactly what we fix. Our platform—
options.feedback: You jumped to the pitch the moment he opened up. The opening was there and you closed it.

options.text: Which one is hurting the P&L more this quarter?
options.feedback: Excellent. You made him prioritise, which tells you what the meeting should be about.

options.text: How many trucks are you running?
options.feedback: Useful data, but it puts the work back on him without showing why it matters to you.

moments.text: "We fix exactly that. Our platform gives you live ETAs, route optimisation, fuel analytics—" "Hold on. I didn't ask for a demo. I asked what this call is about."

options.text: Sorry — let me start over. What does a late delivery actually cost you?
options.feedback: Good recovery. You stopped selling and started listening, which is the only way back.

options.text: Right, but the demo is ten minutes and it'll answer everything.
options.feedback: You pushed a demo after he told you not to. Rapport is now gone and he is looking for an exit.

options.text: Fair enough. I'll email you some information instead.
options.feedback: You gave up the call instead of earning it back. Most replies to that email never come.

moments.text: "Fuel, easily. We're spending about 18% more per kilometre than last year and I can't tell which routes are bleeding it."

options.text: Do you know which routes are worst, or is it invisible right now?
options.feedback: Excellent. You surfaced a specific, measurable gap — that is what a good meeting is built on.

options.text: 18% is a lot. We can bring that down.
options.feedback: Probably true, but unsupported. You claimed an outcome before you had evidence.

options.text: Have you looked at your fuel card data?
options.feedback: Reasonable direction, but you are telling him how to do his job before you have earned it.

options.text: It tells me whether the problem is big enough to justify a change.
options.feedback: Honest, but blunt. He now feels sized up rather than understood.

options.text: Because at 42 trucks, a 3% fuel saving is real money. Is that worth fifteen minutes?
options.feedback: Strong. You quantified the stakes in his terms and converted it into a next step.

options.text: Just trying to understand your setup.
options.feedback: Vague. He will read that as a script and disengage.

moments.text: "We already use a TMS. Been with them three years."

options.text: Then I'm probably wasting your time. Thanks for—
options.feedback: You accepted the brush-off immediately. Most deals die exactly here, and they die quietly.

options.text: Makes sense. What's the one thing it still doesn't do well?
options.feedback: Textbook. You turned a wall into a door without attacking his existing choice.

options.text: We're much better than them.
options.feedback: Unprovable and insulting to his judgement. He chose that vendor and you just called it a mistake.

moments.text: "Look, just send me an email and I'll look at it."

options.text: Sure — what should I put in the subject line so it doesn't get lost?
options.feedback: Clever. You got a small commitment that makes the email far more likely to be opened.

options.text: Happy to. I'll send it today.
options.feedback: Polite, but you handed control to his inbox, which is where most follow-ups go to die.

options.text: I will — but could I ask one thing first? What would make you take a meeting?
options.feedback: Excellent. You traded the email for information, which is a far better deal for you.

moments.text: "And what does this cost? Give me a number."

options.text: It depends on trucks and modules — roughly ₹4,000 per truck per month.
options.feedback: A number is fine, but you priced before value was established. He is now anchored on cost.

options.text: Before I quote, what's that 18% fuel gap costing you monthly?
options.feedback: Strong. You anchored price against his loss instead of your cost, which is how margin survives.

options.text: I'll have to get back to you on pricing.
options.feedback: You lost credibility at the exact moment he tested you. He will assume it is expensive.

moments.text: "We tried something like this in 2023. It was a mess. Why are you different?"

options.text: We're not like them — our product actually works.
options.feedback: Empty claim. He has heard that sentence from every vendor who has ever called him.

options.text: What went wrong in 2023? If it's the same failure, I'll tell you honestly.
options.feedback: Excellent. Honesty plus diagnosis is how trust gets built after a bad experience.

options.text: Every vendor says that, I know. But we have 40 logistics clients.
options.feedback: Social proof helps, but you did not address the scar he just showed you.

moments.text: "Even if I liked it, I'd have to get my CFO and the ops head involved."

options.text: Great — can you get them on the next call?
options.feedback: Useful intent, but you are asking him to do your work without giving him a reason.

options.text: Understood. What would each of them need to see to say yes?
options.feedback: Excellent. You mapped the actual decision criteria before you ever met them.

options.text: No problem, I'll send a proposal for them.
options.feedback: You are now selling to an inbox, not a committee. Proposals without a champion stall.

moments.text: "Alright. I've got a few minutes left. What are you proposing?"

options.text: Thursday 11am, thirty minutes, you and your ops head — I'll bring the route-level fuel analysis.
options.feedback: Perfect close: specific, scoped, and tied directly to the pain he described.

options.text: Whenever works for you — just let me know.
options.feedback: You handed him the decision and the calendar. In practice, nothing will happen.

options.text: Let me send over a deck first.
options.feedback: A deck is a delay tactic. You had momentum and you spent it on homework.

options.text: Monday 10am works. I'll send the invite now, with one line on what I'll bring.
options.feedback: Clean. Confirmed, documented, and set up for a real conversation rather than a chat.

options.text: Monday's fine.
options.feedback: Confirmed, but thin. No agenda, no anchor, and a higher chance he cancels.

options.text: Monday doesn't work for me — Thursday is better.
options.feedback: You made his constraint about you. Unnecessary friction at the finish line.
